documents.body:
OUTSIDE ENDOCRINOLOGY
Visit 01/14/2025
Seen after her October admission for desmopressin-related hyponatremia. Since discharge on desmopressin 0.1 mg twice daily she has had mild daytime thirst and gets up once a night; she prefers this to any further dose change. No headaches or confusion.
Sodium 138.
Plan: keep desmopressin 0.1 mg twice daily. Any future dose change will be paired with a sodium check in 3-5 days. Return in 6 months.

events.reason: Acute shortness of breath, pulmonary edema

reports.text: Portable AP chest. Heart size within normal limits. Pulmonary venous congestion with diffuse interstitial edema. No pleural effusion or pneumothorax. No focal consolidation.
reports.conclusion: Pulmonary venous congestion and interstitial edema.

reports.text: Sinus tachycardia, rate about 110. Normal axis and intervals. No ST-segment elevation or depression.

Left ventricle normal in size with hyperdynamic systolic function, LVEF 65%. No regional wall motion abnormality. Flail segment of the posterior mitral leaflet with ruptured chordae; eccentric, anteriorly directed jet of severe mitral regurgitation. Left atrium not dilated. Aortic valve normal. Right ventricle normal in size and function. No pericardial effusion.
reports.conclusion: Severe acute mitral regurgitation from a flail posterior leaflet segment due to chordal rupture. LVEF 65%, LV not dilated.

reports.text: Post mitral valve repair with annuloplasty ring. Ring well seated. Trace residual mitral regurgitation, no stenosis. LV normal in size, LVEF 60%. No pericardial effusion.
reports.conclusion: Satisfactory mitral repair with trace residual MR. LVEF 60%.

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL - DISCHARGE SUMMARY (Cardiology / Cardiac Surgery)
Admitted 04/18/2025 via the ED to the cardiac ICU. Discharged 04/29/2025.

Presentation: about two hours into an afternoon of gardening she developed sudden, severe breathlessness, could not lie flat, and felt her heart racing. Background: type 2 diabetes, hypertension, central DI on desmopressin, endometrial cancer treated in 2020, desmopressin-related hyponatremia (SIADH) in 2024.
Allergies: lisinopril (angioedema), sulfa (rash).

On arrival: RR 28, BP 150/90, HR 110. Crackles to the mid lung fields on both sides. A new holosystolic apical murmur radiating to the axilla.
Troponin I <0.04; BNP 900; creatinine 1.1; BUN 18.
Chest film: pulmonary venous congestion with interstitial edema. ECG: sinus tachycardia, no ST changes.
Echo: severe mitral regurgitation from a flail posterior leaflet segment with ruptured chordae; LVEF 65%; LV not dilated.

Hospital course: IV furosemide and overnight bilevel positive airway pressure, with rapid improvement in breathing. Coronary angiography 04/20: no obstructive coronary artery disease. Cardiac surgery performed mitral valve repair on 04/22/2025 (resection of the flail posterior segment and annuloplasty ring). Uncomplicated recovery. Post-operative echo 04/26: trace residual MR, LVEF 60%. Sodium monitored closely given her DI; desmopressin continued at her usual dose with no hyponatremia.

Discharge diagnosis: acute severe mitral regurgitation from chordal rupture, status post mitral valve repair.
Discharge medications: aspirin 81 mg daily (3 months after repair, cardiology to review); furosemide 20 mg daily for 2 weeks then stop; metformin 1000 mg twice daily; hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily; desmopressin 0.1 mg twice daily.
Follow-up: PCP in 1-2 weeks; cardiology and cardiac surgery clinic in 3 months with echo. Sternal precautions for 6 weeks.

documents.title: Post-hospital visit - mitral valve repair
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
One week home after an 11-day admission: sudden pulmonary edema from a ruptured mitral chord, repaired surgically 4/22. Discharge paperwork not yet received; reviewed her copy of the discharge medication list and the daughter's account.

Feels stronger each day. Walking around the block twice daily. No shortness of breath lying flat, no palpitations, no fever. Sternal incision a little sore. On furosemide through the end of this week, then done. Aspirin daily per cardiology.

Exam: BP 134/84. Afebrile. Sternotomy incision clean, dry, edges well approximated, no redness. Heart regular, no murmur heard. Lungs clear to the bases. No leg edema.

A/P
1. Acute mitral regurgitation from chordal rupture, s/p repair - doing well. Finish furosemide as directed. Aspirin 81 daily until cardiology review at 3 months. Sternal precautions.
2. Central DI - sodium today given the diuretic and recent admission.
3. HTN - HCTZ.
4. T2DM - metformin; A1c at next visit.
Requested hospital records.

documents.title: Cardiology follow-up
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE CARDIOLOGY
Visit 07/22/2025

Three months after mitral valve repair for acute severe MR due to chordal rupture. She has recovered fully, walks daily, and has no breathlessness, chest pain or palpitations.
Exam: regular rhythm, no murmur. Lungs clear. No edema. Sternum stable.
Echo today: intact repair, trace MR, LVEF 60%.
Plan: aspirin stopped as of today. Repeat echo in one year. Allergies: lisinopril (angioedema), sulfa (rash).

documents.title: Cardiology letter filed

documents.body: Cardiology letter from 7/22 received. Aspirin removed from med list per letter. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: Annual physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
62 y/o for yearly physical. Busy year: valve repair in April, fully recovered, aspirin stopped by cardiology in July. Gardening again. Eye exam in June - she says unchanged; no letter here. No vaginal bleeding. DI stable on 0.1 mg BID; no sodium trouble since last fall.

Exam: BMI 31. Well. Skin: faint acanthosis at the neck. HEENT and neck normal. Heart regular, no murmur, healed sternotomy. Lungs clear. Abdomen benign. No edema. Feet: monofilament intact, pulses palpable. Breast exam deferred - she prefers to rely on the mammogram.

A/P
1. T2DM with mild NPDR - metformin; labs today.
2. HTN on HCTZ - stable.
3. S/p mitral repair - cardiology yearly echo.
4. Central DI / prior desmopressin hyponatremia - sodium today.
5. Hx endometrial cancer - annual pelvic exams with gyn.
6. HM: flu today; COVID at pharmacy. Mammogram ordered. Colonoscopy due next year (2016 normal) - will refer at next visit. PHQ-2 0.
RTC 5 months.

reports.text: Bilateral screening mammogram with tomosynthesis. Compared with 2022 to 2024. Scattered fibroglandular density. No suspicious mass, grouped calcifications or distortion. Sternotomy wires noted at the edge of the field.

events.reason: Postmenopausal vaginal bleeding, history of endometrial cancer

documents.title: Gynecology visit
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GYNECOLOGY
Visit 04/23/2026

Ms. Fairbanks returns to us six years after her endometrial cancer was found here on biopsy; she had staging hysterectomy with BSO in 2020 (stage IA, grade 1) and has been followed since. For about three months she has noticed on-and-off vaginal bleeding, light. She had no bleeding at all from the 2020 surgery until this. No pelvic pain, no weight loss, no change in bowel habits.

Medications: metformin, hydrochlorothiazide, desmopressin. Allergies: lisinopril (angioedema), sulfa (rash). Family history: mother with endometrial cancer.

Exam: BP 132/86. BMI 31. Speculum: small amount of blood in the vaginal vault; cuff closed without a visible lesion. Bimanual: no palpable masses; no adnexal tenderness or masses.
Labs: hemoglobin 12.1, platelets 250, fasting glucose 146, creatinine 0.9.

Impression: postmenopausal bleeding after hysterectomy for endometrial cancer; recurrence at the vaginal cuff must be excluded.
Plan: CT chest, abdomen and pelvis; referred back to gynecologic oncology for examination and biopsy of the cuff.

documents.title: Bleeding again
documents.author: patient
documents.body: I wanted you to know I've had some spotting off and on since around January and saw the gynecologist yesterday. She wants a CT scan and a biopsy with the cancer doctor to make sure it's not back. I'm nervous. CT is May 7.

documents.title: RE: Bleeding again
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thank you for telling me, Donna. Checking carefully is exactly the right step, and your cancer was found early and treated completely in 2020. Please have the gynecologist's office send us their note and any results. Call or message any time if you want to talk it through.

reports.text: Specimen: vaginal cuff, biopsy. Fragments of benign squamous mucosa with chronic inflammation. No dysplasia. No malignancy identified.
reports.conclusion: Vaginal cuff biopsy: benign squamous mucosa with chronic inflammation; negative for malignancy.

documents.title: Gynecologic oncology - cuff biopsy
documents.author: gynecologic oncology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GYNECOLOGIC ONCOLOGY
Visit 05/19/2026

Seen for intermittent vaginal bleeding six years after surgery for stage IA endometrioid endometrial cancer. CT chest, abdomen and pelvis on 05/07/2026 showed no evidence of recurrent or metastatic disease.
Exam: no adenopathy. Abdomen benign. Speculum: cuff intact without a visible lesion; biopsies of the cuff taken. Rectovaginal exam without nodularity.
Pathology: benign squamous mucosa with chronic inflammation; no malignancy.
Impression: no evidence of recurrent endometrial cancer.
Plan: re-examine in 3 months, sooner if bleeding increases.
Allergies: lisinopril (angioedema), sulfa (rash).

documents.title: Update
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Good news so far - the cancer doctor said my CT on the 7th was clear. She took a small biopsy yesterday and will call with it next week. Fingers crossed.

documents.title: RE: Update
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: That's very reassuring - thanks for the update. We haven't received the CT report; I'll ask their office to send it along with the biopsy result.
